title: Same-directory fork lifecycle transport test for KCH R11
governing_objective: Determine whether a new Codex task forked into the already configured R11 workspace loads or executes KCH interposition before its first new substantive turn.

historical_dependency.use: verified isolated installation and host lifecycle failure localization only

activation_gate: child task resolves to the configured source workspace
activation evidence originates after child creation and before source-thread reading
evidence names an actually executed KCH hook, MCP preflight, or native approval request
copied parent history and static configuration files do not count as activation
no KCH instruction is added to the common task prompt
stop_rules: If the child does not share the configured directory, mark condition FAIL.
If a trust or approval request appears, preserve it and wait for the user; do not self-approve.
If no child-session activation evidence precedes substantive work, mark automatic activation FAIL even if the task answer is otherwise good.
Do not treat this transport-only case as a blinded causal efficacy comparison.
Do not mutate the native source thread or run PHL real.
